summary: UNION stacks the results of two queries, one on top of the other.
points: Both queries must return the same number of columns in a matching order.
UNION removes duplicate rows, and UNION ALL keeps them.
Column names come from the first query.
In SQLite, ORDER BY goes once at the very end, and you can't put brackets around each branch.

example.sql:
SELECT name, 'Customer' AS kind FROM customers
UNION ALL
SELECT name, 'Product' FROM products
ORDER BY kind, name;
example.explanation: This combines two lists into one, with a label showing where each row came from.
